requirement: The Habeas crate MUST use the same `habeas::validate()` Cargo integration test as downstream projects to check its own requirements and evidence.
rationale:
structural: The text has one structural obligation: "The Habeas crate MUST use the same `habeas::validate()` Cargo integration test as downstream projects to check its own requirements and evidence." This fixes two things: the check is a Cargo integration test, and it is done by calling `habeas::validate()` rather than by a separate self-checking routine. A different implementation would run its own validation logic, or call something other than `habeas::validate()`. That could produce the same results and would still violate the clause, so the obligation is structural.

The supplied root `tests/habeas.rs#fn[habeas]` meets it. It is a `#[test]` function in the `tests/` directory, so Cargo builds it as an integration test. Its entire body is `habeas::validate();`. It carries both `{impl}` and `{test}` markers for `requirements.integration.self_test`. I found no other structural clause to map, and no further root is needed. Whether `validate()` behaves correctly is covered by `requirements.integration.validate` and is outside this subject.
